clue.text: Councillor on water at Oxford having a difficult time

parts.note: the Isis is the name the Thames goes by as it flows through Oxford

explanation.surface: A local councillor out rowing on the river at Oxford is struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: The ISIS is the stretch of the River Thames at Oxford, where the university rows. The definition 'having a difficult time' is read as 'a time of difficulty'.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning point of acute trouble is exactly a difficult time.

clue.text: Introduction to Isaiah in a volume used in religious instruction course?

indicators.note: used in means placed inside, so the rest sits between the two letters

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, a school subject

indicators.note: in means the first letter goes inside the words for a volume
the introduction to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A scripture lesson that begins with a book of Isaiah.
explanation.walkthrough: I (introduction to Isaiah) goes into A VOL, giving AVIOL, which is 'used in' RI (religious instruction). 'Course' looks like the school course, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasta dish served as one stage of a meal is a course.

clue.text: Immunising agents turned up in nuclear establishment

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Vaccines are discovered at a nuclear research site.
explanation.walkthrough: In nucleAR ESt are the letters ARES; in a down clue, 'turned up' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood serums carrying antibodies are used to give immunity.

clue.text: Sporting activities only possible well above the snowline?

definitions.text: Sporting activities only possible well above the snowline?

parts.words: Sporting activities only possible well above the snowline?
parts.note: suggests mountaineering, but the sport leaves the snow to fly high above it

explanation.surface: Sports that can be done only high in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Above the snowline' suggests altitude; the jumpers in this event fly well above the snow itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In this winter event, competitors leap from a ramp and fly high over the snow.

clue.text: A tax on credit for menswear item

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the tax pieces come after the credit

parts.note: CR is the usual abbreviation for credit in accounts
VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax

explanation.surface: Someone buys a tie on credit and pays tax on it.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT (value added tax) is the British sales tax. 'On' tells you A and VAT come after CR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a neck scarf worn by men, so it is an item of male clothing.

clue.text: Prairie dweller's old toy turning up in church

indicators.note: in means these letters are placed inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: An old toy belonging to someone from the prairies is found in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: TOY 'turning up' gives YOT; with O (old) it goes inside CE (Church of England). The 's is a link, 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: This wild dog of North America lives on the open grasslands.

clue.text: Animal burrowing in wood, one exhibited by museum

parts.note: ash is a kind of tree and its timber
a mole is a burrowing animal
an means one

explanation.surface: A mole digs into a piece of wood that a museum puts on show.
explanation.walkthrough: MOLE is 'burrowing in' ASH; AN (one) follows. The Ashmolean is Oxford's museum of art and archaeology.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashmolean in Oxford is a famous gallery of art and antiquities.

clue.text: Help to catch flightless bird, stupid creature

indicators.note: to catch means to hold, so the help word goes around the bird

parts.note: aid means help
the rhea is a large flightless bird of South America

explanation.surface: Lending a hand to capture a bird that cannot fly, a foolish animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The RHEA is a South American flightless bird; AID catches it.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty-headed person is a fool, a stupid creature.

clue.text: Break new ground, as pearl-fisher penning poem in Seychelles?

parts.note: pearl-fishers dive for oysters, so one is a diver

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the country code holds the poem inside it

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: A pearl diver writes verse while working in the Seychelles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If—' is Kipling's best-known poem, and SY is the Seychelles' vehicle registration code. 'Penning' puts IF inside SY. The wordplay and the verb definition both give DIVERSIFY; the grid as printed has DIVERSITY, one letter off.
explanation.definitionFit: To branch out into new activities is to break new ground.

clue.text: Tories elude development that's potentially damaging

indicators.note: a development is a change, so the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A political story in which the Conservatives dodge a harmful development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' rearranges TORIES ELUDE. Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deleterious is harmful, capable of doing damage.

clue.text: Tough restriction placed on classical art by Pope?

indicators.note: a restriction hems something in, so the Pope's letters close around the Latin word

parts.note: HH stands for His Holiness, the title of the Pope
ars is the Latin, so classical, word for art

explanation.surface: The Pope limits what can be done with ancient art, which seems a hard line.
explanation.walkthrough: HH (His Holiness) is the Pope; ARS is Latin for art, hence 'classical'. The restriction puts ARS between the two Hs. 'Pope' might bring Alexander Pope the poet to mind, but here it is the pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh treatment is severe and rough, which is to say tough.

clue.text: Great admiration for priestess associated with divine service

indicators.note: associated with puts the two pieces side by side

parts.note: Hero was the priestess of Aphrodite in the legend of Hero and Leander
worship is a religious service

explanation.surface: A priestess is linked to religious worship.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend Hero was a priestess of Aphrodite, loved by Leander. 'Priestess' is not a woman hero here but a named one.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolising someone is having great admiration for them.

clue.text: A sign one's a celebrity

definitions.meaning: Leo, the ..., is a sign of the zodiac
a literary ... or social ... is a much-feted famous person

explanation.surface: Something that shows you have become famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is a link: 'a sign' is the fifth sign of the zodiac, Leo, and a lion is also a feted celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo's emblem is that beast, and a socialite who is lionised is a fêted star.

clue.text: Lots of people go through his rooms

definitions.text: Lots of people go through his rooms

parts.words: Lots of people go through his rooms
parts.note: read as crowds passing through someone's premises, but the lots are items for sale passing through a saleroom

explanation.surface: His premises see a lot of people pass through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' reads as 'many', but here lots are items put up for sale, and the rooms are salerooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who runs sales sells one lot after another in the salerooms.

clue.text: Exhaust American with exercise after running one lap it appears?

indicators.note: the exercise letters follow the mixed-up group
running suggests movement and change, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: An American jogger tires himself out after running a lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' mixes I (one), LAP and IT into TAILPI; PE (physical education) comes 'after' it. 'Exhaust' reads as a verb meaning tire, but it is the noun: the US word for an exhaust pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a car's exhaust pipe by this name, so it is the US term for an exhaust.

clue.text: Document drawn up by clever people, in part

indicators.note: in means the clever people sit inside the letters for part

parts.note: arch means cunning, clever
men means people

explanation.surface: A paper written by smart people, partly.
explanation.walkthrough: ARCH (cunning) and MEN go inside PT (part). 'Drawn up by' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is a written document on treated animal skin.

clue.text: Provide funds for friend owing quite a bit?

indicators.note: quite a bit of the two words, but not all, gives the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: A friend who owes a large sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in friEND OWing: 'quite a bit' says only part of the words is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an institution a lasting income is to provide money for it.

clue.text: Prepare for hostilities when one's in US port

indicators.note: in means the one's letters go inside the port's name

parts.note: Mobile is a port in Alabama
one is I in Roman numerals, and the 's adds the S, read as 'one is'

explanation.surface: Getting ready for war when one is in an American harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Mobile is a seaport in Alabama; IS ('one's' read as I + S, 'one is') goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To mobilise troops is to get them ready to go to war.

clue.text: Step up for bishop holding one Episcopal office — almost

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the bishop's letters go around the rest

parts.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
one is I in Roman numerals

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a see is a bishop's office or diocese

explanation.surface: A bishop is moving toward a higher post in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) is a bishop's title. A bishop's office is his SEE; 'almost' cuts it to SE. 'Holding' puts I and SE inside RR. A riser is the vertical part of a stair.
explanation.definitionFit: On a staircase, the riser is the upright part of each step, the part that rises.

clue.text: An academic pupil

definitions.meaning: a pupil at school, in the older sense

explanation.surface: An academic student.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned academic, and also, in older use, a schoolchild.

clue.text: Light nap for Parisian cats and dogs?

parts.note: down is light, soft fluff, like the nap on cloth
pour is the French for 'for'

explanation.surface: A short doze for someone in Paris, with a mention of pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light nap' reads as a short sleep, but nap here is a fabric's fluffy surface, and soft fluff is DOWN. POUR is French for 'for'. To rain cats and dogs is to rain very heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Raining cats and dogs is an idiom for very heavy rain, a deluge.

clue.text: Row about comfortable accommodation having rather low rating?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the row word surrounds the cosy home

parts.note: to row is to oar
a nest is a snug home

explanation.surface: A complaint about cosy lodgings that have a poor review.
explanation.walkthrough: OAR goes 'about' NEST. 'Row' suggests an argument, but it is rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel or review with a single star ranks near the bottom of the scale.

clue.text: Hired hand?

parts.note: reads as a labourer, but hand here is applause, and it is paid for

explanation.surface: A farm labourer taken on for wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' is applause, as in 'give her a big hand'; theatres once paid a group to clap.
explanation.definitionFit: A claque is a group paid to applaud in a theatre.

clue.text: Concerned with the performance of pupils etc?

definitions.text: Concerned with the performance of pupils etc?

parts.words: Concerned with the performance of pupils etc?
parts.note: reads like a school report, but pupils are also the dark centres of the eyes

explanation.surface: Something to do with how well schoolchildren are doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupils' suggests schoolchildren, but here they are the parts of the eye; 'etc' covers the rest of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical word for anything to do with the eyes, such as how pupils react to light.

clue.text: Entering border the wrong way, leader of smuggling network

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the leading letter goes into the turned border
the wrong way means the word for border is read backwards

parts.note: a hem is the folded border of cloth

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The head of a smuggling ring crosses the frontier illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: HEM (a border on cloth) read 'the wrong way' gives MEH, and 'leader of smuggling', S, enters it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesh is a net-like web of threads, which is a network.

clue.text: Runner died in motoring mishap

parts.note: a ski is the runner on which one glides over snow

explanation.surface: An athlete died in a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete, but a ski is a runner, like a sledge's.
explanation.definitionFit: Sliding out of control on a slippery road is a mishap when driving.

clue.text: Crack appears in part of shoe when going around Vatican

indicators.note: going around means the shoe part encloses the letter for Vatican

parts.note: the sole is the underside of a shoe
V is the international vehicle code for Vatican City

explanation.surface: A crack opens in the sole of a shoe while walking around the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the Vatican City vehicle code. 'Crack' looks like the split in the shoe, but it is the definition: to crack a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a code or problem is to work it out.

clue.text: Question involving pickets would lead to this measure

indicators.note: a reworking of the letters is what leads to the answer, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A query about striking pickets would bring about this step.
explanation.walkthrough: QU (question) with PICKETS makes nine letters, rearranged as 'would lead to this' says. 'Measure' is a dance measure, not a policy step.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance in quick time is a measure in the old sense of a dance.

clue.text: Flaunting her wit -it makes you squirm

indicators.note: flaunting means showing off with a flourish, so the letters are paraded in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who shows off how clever she is will make others cringe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flaunting' reorders HER WIT. 'It makes you' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and wriggle, which is how one squirms.

clue.text: Last object to be found beside river

indicators.note: beside puts the river right next to the object, after it

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose, an object
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: The final item is discovered near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire. 'Last' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb, meaning to go on.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to go on enduring, to hold out over time.
